findings.evidence: Spec 5 design text contains the literal 'Alt+Tab', which contradicts the spec's own judge grep (section 10) that must find no 'Alt+Tab' in the four files. The wording keeps the meaning (names macOS Full Keyboard Access as the cause) and satisfies the grep.
findings.fix: None needed; the spec says 'wording may vary, content fixed'. Optionally note the deviation in the final summary.

summary: All SPEC items implemented as designed. keyboard.ts matches the interface exactly (Tab then Alt+Tab, no Alt+Tab call when Tab succeeds, exact error message, probe page closed in finally). The probe runs on a separate page in the same context using setContent only; every addInitScript/route/request listener in the four files is page-scoped, the context-wide clock does not matter for focus/keypress on static HTML, and src/ has no blur/visibilitychange/hasFocus listeners that a new page could trigger. The SPEC-02 test would catch probing on `page` itself (input focus and content lost), a leaked probe page (page count), and Chromium returning Alt+Tab; the SPEC-02b test would catch wrong order, an extra Alt+Tab call, and a missing throw. Locked files: assertion counts via doit ASSERT_RE are unchanged at 30/8/22/41, and the multiset of expect lines (excluding the expectErrorScreen call-site signature change) is identical before and after, so nothing was added, removed or loosened. grep for 'Alt+Tab|browserName' in the four files finds nothing. Local re-run of keyboard-helper + back-focus on both projects: 10 passed. Gate fix-2 passes (full e2e 421 passed, lint, typecheck, budget 126/130 lines, 6/6 files).
